## Overview

The plugins-copilot-cross-engine-audit (audit-report.md:105-111, commit `f4d63067`) filed FAIL row `copilot-skill-mirror-parity`: the `implement-with-ralph` Copilot mirror at `plugins/ralph/.copilot-plugin/copilot-skills/implement-with-ralph/SKILL.md` still contains 33 references to deleted bash shims (`codex-exec.sh`, `copilot-exec.sh`, `ralph.sh`, `drain-cascade.sh`, `review-loop.sh`, `lib/parse-not-tested-trailers.sh`) after the v5.46.0 all-Node migration. Operators copying commands from the mirror will hit "no such file or directory."

The mirror is a **hand-fork** — explicitly excluded from `generate-copilot-artifacts.mjs --write` (see `scripts/generate-copilot-artifacts.mjs:37` `USER_SKILLS` list) because it carries Copilot-specific divergences (async polling, marker-file fallback). Running the generator alone will not fix it; both the Claude source AND the Copilot mirror must be hand-edited in lockstep. The Claude source carries 38 `.sh\b` hits — those must be cleaned too, otherwise the next lockstep edit re-introduces staleness.

A regression check must be added so the next migration cannot ship without auditing the implement-with-ralph mirror. The existing parity gate `scripts/check-copilot-parity.mjs` already enforces five assertions (A–E); this plan adds **Assertion F: no `.sh\b` references in the `implement-with-ralph` source-or-mirror SKILL.md** (with an `parity-exceptions.json` mechanism for justified survivors).

This work targets the sibling repo at `D:/ai-developer-toolkit/` (NOT codexu). Per `feedback_impl_topic_branch_vs_lead_branch`, the impl member cuts a topic branch `ralph/ralph-implement-with-ralph-copilot-mirror-regenerate` off `origin/main` of the **plugin repo** (not codexu). #### `ralph.sh` reword playbook

Apply these contextual rewordings in BOTH surfaces. Use Grep + Edit on each hit, not a sed-style replace_all — context matters for some hits.

| Old prose pattern | New prose | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| `passed through to ralph.sh` | `passed through to the ralph runner` | conceptual reference |
| `Run ralph.sh via Bash` | `Run the ralph runner via Bash` (and update the command body to `node "<plugin_root>/src/ralph.mjs" ...`) | literal invocation |
| `1 iteration per ralph.sh run` / `3 iterations per ralph.sh run` | `1 iteration per ralph run` / `3 iterations per ralph run` | system name |
| `ralph.sh init_job_state()` / `ralph.sh tracks job state` | `ralph's init_job_state()` (or `src/ralph.mjs init_job_state()`) | API reference |
| `worktree-aware, same as ralph.sh` | `worktree-aware, same as src/ralph.mjs` | path reference |
| `ralph.sh --engine` | `ralph runner --engine` | flag context |
| `via codex-exec.sh` / `via copilot-exec.sh` | `via src/codex-exec.mjs` / `via src/copilot-exec.mjs` | path reference |
| `the review-loop.sh pattern` | `the review-loop pattern (in src/review-loop.mjs)` | pattern ref |
| `scripts/drain-cascade.sh` | `scripts/drain-cascade.mjs` | path |
| `lib/parse-not-tested-trailers.sh` | `src/parse-not-tested-trailers.mjs` | path |

Any other hit not matching the table: hand-decide using the surrounding sentence. Aim for present-tense, current-code-accurate prose. If a reference is purely historical (e.g., "previously the .sh shim..."), strip the sentence entirely rather than rewording — it doesn't belong in present-tense skill prose.

#### Assertion F design (US-003)

Extend `scripts/check-copilot-parity.mjs`. The current script (verified 2026-05-28):
- Imports `fs/promises` only (no sync `fs`) — every read must `await fs.readFile(...)`.
- Runs `main().catch(...)` unconditionally at the bottom, so importing it from a test currently re-runs the full CLI. **US-003 must refactor the script to add a CLI guard matching the pattern already used in `scripts/generate-copilot-artifacts.mjs` (script tail)** so a test can `import { assertNoStaleShRefs }` without triggering `main()`.
- Exports nothing. **US-003 must export `assertNoStaleShRefs` (and any other helpers needed by the test)**.

Required refactor — add this near the bottom of `check-copilot-parity.mjs` (replacing the bare `main().catch(...)` block):

```javascript
const argvPath = process.argv[1] ? path.resolve(process.argv[1]).replace(/\\/g, '/') : '';
const modulePath = decodeURIComponent(import.meta.url.replace(/^file:\/\//, '').replace(/^\/([A-Za-z]:)/, '$1')).replace(/\\/g, '/');
if (argvPath && modulePath.endsWith(argvPath)) {
  main().catch((error) => {
    console.error(error.message);
    process.exit(1);
  });
}
```

Add `export` to `assertNoStaleShRefs` (and any callers it needs).

New assertion (uses async `fs/promises` — the existing module style):

```javascript
// Assertion F: no .sh\b refs in implement-with-ralph source/mirror.
// Exception schema: parity-exceptions.json `staleShAllowList` is an array of
//   { "path": "<repo-relative path>", "line": <1-based int>, "reason": "<text>" }
// objects. The check compares `${rel}:${line}` strings against an internal Set
// built from the structured entries.
export async function assertNoStaleShRefs(repoRoot, exceptions) {
  const targets = [
    'plugins/ralph/skills/implement-with-ralph/SKILL.md',
    'plugins/ralph/.copilot-plugin/copilot-skills/implement-with-ralph/SKILL.md',
  ];
  const allowList = Array.isArray(exceptions.staleShAllowList) ? exceptions.staleShAllowList : [];
  const allowed = new Set(allowList.map((entry) => `${entry.path}:${entry.line}`));
  const failures = [];
  for (const rel of targets) {
    const text = await fs.readFile(path.join(repoRoot, rel), 'utf8');
    const lines = text.split('\n');
    lines.forEach((line, idx) => {
      if (/\.sh\b/.test(line) && !allowed.has(`${rel}:${idx + 1}`)) {
        failures.push(`${rel}:${idx + 1}: ${line.trim()}`);
      }
    });
  }
  if (failures.length) {
    fail('Assertion F', `stale .sh refs:\n${failures.join('\n')}`);
  }
}
```

Wire it into `main()` alongside the existing assertions (after `await assertionE()`):
```javascript
await assertNoStaleShRefs(repoRoot, exceptions);
```

`exceptions` is the already-parsed `parity-exceptions.json` object that `main()` reads near the top.

Schema extension in `.copilot-plugin/parity-exceptions.json` (strict JSON — no comments allowed; use a sibling `staleShAllowListNotes` field on the rare occasion that contextual notes are needed):
```json
{
  "source": "plugins/ralph/docs/future-work/copilot-hand-fork-exceptions-2026-05-17.md",
  "probeResults": "plugins/ralph/docs/future-work/copilot-probe-results.md",
  "headerExceptions": [ /* existing entries unchanged */ ],
  "staleShAllowList": []
}
```

Initial value: empty array. Each future entry has shape `{"path": "plugins/ralph/.../SKILL.md", "line": 123, "reason": "fixture stub kept intentionally"}`.

#### Testing strategy

Two options considered:

- **Option A (recommended): new `tests/test-no-stale-sh-refs.mjs`** — small focused **node:test** (`import { test } from 'node:test'`; `import assert from 'node:assert/strict'`) that imports `assertNoStaleShRefs` from the refactored parity script and exercises three cases:
  1. **Happy path** — points the function at the real `repoRoot` (`process.cwd()` from the test runs at the worktree root; the test resolves the repo root via `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` for portability) with the live empty allowlist and asserts it resolves without throwing.
  2. **Injected hit not in allowlist** — writes a fixture SKILL.md under `os.tmpdir()/test-no-stale-sh-refs-<pid>/plugins/ralph/skills/implement-with-ralph/SKILL.md` containing a literal `codex-exec.sh` line, runs with empty `staleShAllowList`, asserts `assertNoStaleShRefs` rejects with a message matching `/Assertion F.*codex-exec\.sh/`.
  3. **Injected hit in allowlist** — same fixture, but `staleShAllowList: [{path: "plugins/ralph/skills/implement-with-ralph/SKILL.md", line: <N>, reason: "test"}]`, asserts it resolves.
  Cleanup: `fs.rm(tmpDir, { recursive: true, force: true })` in a `test.after()`.
- **Option B: extend `tests/test-copilot-generator.sh`** — adds a sub-case at the end. Rejected because the bash test is being phased out (the v5.46.0 migration moved the bulk of tests to node:test) and because the bash test only exercises the generator, not the parity check.

**Chosen: Option A.** Add `tests/test-no-stale-sh-refs.mjs`. The auto-discovery harness `tests/run.mjs` picks up files matching `/^test-.*\.mjs$/`, so no registration edit is needed.

## Risk Areas

1. **Lockstep drift between Claude source and Copilot mirror.** US-002 must preserve every Copilot-specific divergence (Phase 3 async polling block, Terminal Marker File Fallback block, Planning engine appendix). Failure mode: a sweeping search-and-replace deletes a Copilot-only section because it mentions `.sh`. Mitigation: hand-Edit each hit, not Grep-then-replace_all; re-run `node plugins/ralph/scripts/check-copilot-parity.mjs` after every edit to catch anchor breakage early.
2. **Misidentifying conceptual `ralph.sh` references as path references.** Some hits like `ralph.sh tracks job state in <job_dir>/job-state.json automatically` are best reworded as `the ralph runner tracks ...`. Others like `passed through to ralph.sh` are flag-passing references. Use the reword playbook table, but expect a few hand-decisions.
3. **Whitespace / line-number reflow.** Edits shift line numbers between Claude source and Copilot mirror. After US-001 ships, the impl member must NOT assume the mirror's line numbers match the table. Re-run `grep -nE '\.sh\b'` on the mirror before US-002.
4. **`parity-exceptions.json` schema extension.** Adding `staleShAllowList` is a schema change. Other consumers of this file (if any) might break. Mitigation: greppingthe repo for `parity-exceptions` references — the only known consumer is `check-copilot-parity.mjs` itself, plus the v5.46.0 plan that mentioned it. Safe to extend.
5. **Five-stamp version-bump drift.** Forgetting one stamp produces a release where one manifest is out of sync. Mitigation: the CHANGELOG v5.46.0 entry lists all five — copy the path list verbatim and grep `grep -rn '5\.46\.0' .claude-plugin .github .agents plugins/ralph/.claude-plugin plugins/ralph/.github` to confirm five hits before bump, five hits after.
6. **No CI workflow exists** (verified 2026-05-28: `D:/ai-developer-toolkit/.github/workflows/` does not exist). Assertion F runs locally via `node plugins/ralph/scripts/check-copilot-parity.mjs` and via the test in `tests/run.mjs`. The impl member MUST run both gates from inside the worktree before pushing (AC-4, AC-6). Adding a CI workflow that runs the parity check is a follow-up — not in scope here.
7. **Multi-remote push: `origin` AND `work`** (verified 2026-05-28). The spawn prompt's "Multi-remote push" instruction is the operator's standing authorization for this task. Use an explicit loop with per-remote assertion:
   ```bash
   FAIL=0
   for r in origin work; do
     if ! git push "$r" HEAD:ralph/ralph-implement-with-ralph-copilot-mirror-regenerate; then
       echo "PUSH FAILED to $r" >&2; FAIL=1
     fi
   done
   test "$FAIL" -eq 0
   ```
   If a remote is unreachable (auth stale, DNS), the impl member surfaces `kind=question` to the lead BEFORE retrying — do not silently swallow the failure.
8. **Codex CLI ENOENT fallback.** Per spawn prompt: if codex iterations hit ENOENT on Windows, set `CODEX_EXEC_SCRIPT` to the v5.44.0 bash wrapper. The wrapper path `D:/ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/ralph/codex-exec.sh` is DELETED in v5.46.0; the fallback only works against a v5.44.0-vintage checkout. **Concrete mitigation:** the impl member first re-tries with the `.mjs` path. If the ENOENT persists on Windows, surface `kind=question` to the lead — do NOT attempt to resurrect the deleted shim in this worktree. The lead can switch to the copilot engine (`--iteration-engine copilot`) as a workaround. Auto-rollback is acceptable per the standard implement-with-ralph contract.
9. **`.worktrees/` not in `D:/ai-developer-toolkit/.gitignore`** (verified 2026-05-28 — only `.claude/worktrees/` is ignored). Without an ignore rule, `git status` from the parent tree shows `?? .worktrees/`. The plan adds `.worktrees/` to the file list (item #11) to silence the noise and reduce the chance of accidentally staging worktree-internal content.

## Preliminary Story Decomposition

5 stories total. US-001 and US-002 are serial (US-002 needs US-001's reword playbook decisions visible to keep both surfaces in sync). US-003 is independent of US-001/US-002 in code but must run after them so its test exercises the cleaned surfaces. US-004 (CHANGELOG + bump) and US-005 (push) are sequential at the end.

### US-001: Reword stale `.sh\b` refs in implement-with-ralph Claude source

**Description:** As a Ralph plugin maintainer, I want the implement-with-ralph Claude source SKILL.md to have zero references to deleted bash shims so operators following the docs hit live `.mjs` paths instead of "no such file or directory."
**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] `grep -cE '\.sh\b' plugins/ralph/skills/implement-with-ralph/SKILL.md` returns `0`
- [ ] Every replacement was made per the reword playbook table; no historical-only `ralph.sh` sentences left over
- [ ] `node plugins/ralph/scripts/check-copilot-parity.mjs` still passes (no H2/H3 headers removed/renamed)
- [ ] `node plugins/ralph/scripts/generate-copilot-artifacts.mjs --check` still passes
**Dependencies:** None
**Estimated complexity:** medium (38 hits, many one-by-one judgments)

### US-002: Reword stale `.sh\b` refs in implement-with-ralph Copilot mirror (lockstep)

**Description:** As a Copilot-CLI user, I want the implement-with-ralph SKILL.md mirror to have zero references to deleted bash shims so the example commands I copy actually work.

**Why US-002 depends on US-001 (not parallel):** The parity gate (`check-copilot-parity.mjs`) asserts that every Claude-source H2/H3 header has a matching Copilot anchor (assertions B/C). If US-001 renames a header that the mirror anchors to (low-risk because the reword playbook touches prose, not headers, but still possible), the mirror anchor breaks. Serializing US-002 after US-001 means US-002 sees the final source headers and can rewrite anchors atomically with the prose edits. US-002 MUST run `node plugins/ralph/scripts/check-copilot-parity.mjs` as its AC to catch any anchor drift before the story commits.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] `grep -cE '\.sh\b' plugins/ralph/.copilot-plugin/copilot-skills/implement-with-ralph/SKILL.md` returns `0`
- [ ] All Copilot-specific divergences preserved (Phase 3 async polling block, Terminal Marker File Fallback block, Planning engine appendix mentioned in parity-exceptions.json:5-20)
- [ ] `node plugins/ralph/scripts/check-copilot-parity.mjs` passes (anchors stay live — assertions A–E green; F is added in US-003)
**Dependencies:** US-001
**Estimated complexity:** medium

### US-003: Add Assertion F (no stale `.sh\b`) + test

**Description:** As a Ralph plugin maintainer, I want the parity gate to refuse a release that re-introduces stale `.sh` refs in either surface of implement-with-ralph, so future migrations cannot regress this row.
**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] `scripts/check-copilot-parity.mjs` has a new `assertNoStaleShRefs(repoRoot, exceptions)` function called from `main()`
- [ ] `parity-exceptions.json` has a `staleShAllowList` field (empty array initially)
- [ ] `tests/test-no-stale-sh-refs.mjs` covers: (a) happy-path zero hits, (b) injected fixture with a hit not in allowlist FAILS, (c) injected fixture with a hit in allowlist PASSES
- [ ] `tests/run.mjs` auto-discovers and runs the new test
- [ ] `node plugins/ralph/tests/test-no-stale-sh-refs.mjs` exits 0
- [ ] `node plugins/ralph/tests/run.mjs` exits 0
**Dependencies:** US-001, US-002 (gate must pass against the cleaned surfaces)
**Estimated complexity:** small

### US-004: Ship v5.46.1 (CHANGELOG + five stamps)

**Description:** As a Ralph plugin consumer, I want a v5.46.1 release that surfaces the mirror-staleness fix and its parity-gate so I can pull the patch via the marketplace.
**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] `CHANGELOG.md` has a v5.46.1 entry at the top matching the template in the plan §"CHANGELOG entry (v5.46.1)"
- [ ] All five release stamps read `5.46.1` (see plan AC-7)
- [ ] No `5.46.0` references remain in the five stamped files
**Dependencies:** US-001, US-002, US-003
**Estimated complexity:** small

### US-005: Multi-remote push + verification re-run

**Description:** As the operator, I want the topic branch pushed to every configured remote, and a final clean-run of the audit's exact grep so the FAIL row would now flip to PASS.
**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] `git remote -v` lists all configured remotes; `git push <remote> HEAD` succeeds for each
- [ ] From the worktree: `grep -nE '\.sh\b' plugins/ralph/.copilot-plugin/copilot-skills/implement-with-ralph/SKILL.md` returns no output (matches the audit's exact PASS criterion)
- [ ] `node plugins/ralph/scripts/check-copilot-parity.mjs` and `node plugins/ralph/scripts/generate-copilot-artifacts.mjs --check` both exit 0 from the worktree
- [ ] Topic branch exists on all remotes
**Dependencies:** US-001, US-002, US-003, US-004
**Estimated complexity:** small

## Suggested Decomposition

Serial across all five stories — every story touches files that downstream stories validate. No parallelism opportunity.

### Cluster: serial-mirror-regenerate
- Stories: US-001, US-002, US-003, US-004, US-005
- Phase: 1
- Depends on: None
- File-overlap evidence: shared=[`plugins/ralph/skills/implement-with-ralph/SKILL.md`, `plugins/ralph/.copilot-plugin/copilot-skills/implement-with-ralph/SKILL.md`, `plugins/ralph/scripts/check-copilot-parity.mjs`, `plugins/ralph/CHANGELOG.md`, five version stamps]; exclusive=[]; risk=high
- `execution_mode` rationale: This cluster must run serially. US-002 reads the source's structure produced by US-001; US-003's test exercises the surfaces from US-001/US-002; US-004 stamps the release that codifies all prior work; US-005 is the push. Splitting US-001 and US-002 to parallel members would race on the parity-check gate (both edits change anchor structure). Tier-1 risk per `docs/parallel-safety.md` — plugin state files and release stamps are strictly serial.

Parallel handoff: `/implement-with-ralph --from-plan D:/harness-efforts/codexu/.ralph/jobs/ralph-implement-with-ralph-copilot-mirror-regenerate/plan.md --parallel --suggested-decomposition D:/harness-efforts/codexu/.ralph/jobs/ralph-implement-with-ralph-copilot-mirror-regenerate/suggested-decomposition.json`
